deities: Vana Durga/Parvati — worshipped in a sacred pit with NO idol; a mirror/thidambu marks the spot
festivals: Thrikkarthika — Karthika day of Vrishchikam (Nov–Dec), the temple's main festival day with annadanam for thousands

history.dynasty: Tradition attributes the first pooja to Adi Shankaracharya; administered by the Malabar Devaswom Board
history.period: Traditionally ~1900 years (flag — traditional claim); sanctum rebuilt in granite after a 1993 Deva Prashna
history.summary: A major Devi temple unique for having no idol: Devi is worshipped in a small sacred pit, believed to be the hole made by Shiva's arrow that summoned Ganga to quench Parvati's thirst (the Kirata–Kiratai legend with Arjuna, who worshipped here seeking the Pasupathastra). Adi Shankaracharya is said to have stopped at this 'invisible wall' during his travels, received the goddess's darshan, and performed the first pooja — so the temple is often described as ~1900 years old, a traditional claim to flag rather than a documented date. The name means 'acacia forest'. The two famous vazhipadus are Poomoodal (covering the pit with thechi flowers, Friday nights) and Muttarukkal (coconut breaking to ward off obstacles — about 30 lakh coconuts are offered yearly). The goddess is worshipped in three forms: Vidhya Durga, Vana Durga and Aadi Durga. CSV town/state (Malappuram, Kerala) are correct; town is Kadampuzha (Melmuri, Tirur taluk).

name: Kadampuzha Devi Temple
town_description: Kadampuzha (Melmuri) is a pilgrim town in Tirur taluk on the Malappuram–Tirur corridor, named from 'kadambu' (acacia) forest; daily life here revolves around the Devi temple.
tradition: Shaktism (Durga/Parvati worship, Shankara tradition); Kerala tantra

travel.railway: Nearest major station: Tirur (verify distance); local bus connectivity
travel.road: Off the Vettichira–Malappuram route, Melmuri, Kadampuzha 676553

visitor_information.best_time: November–January (Thrikkarthika, Rigveda Laksharchana); Tuesdays, Fridays, Sundays are special
visitor_information.opening_hours: 4:30 AM–12:00 noon and 3:30 PM–7:00 PM; Muttarukkal 5:00–7:00 AM only; Poomoodal 9:00–11:00 AM (timings subject to change during renovation/festivals). Only Hindus in the main temple; traditional dress code (mundu, no shirts in nalambalam)
